summary: A pristine tree was extracted from the baseline commit of the staged snapshot and the exported diff was checked with git apply --check and then applied; application succeeded with only a benign file-mode warning (executable bit versus regular), and the resulting source file hash matched the working repaired copy exactly. The full discriminator replay on the freshly patched tree produced no credential on the plaintext hop, a regression matrix with zero failing wire cases and zero failing predicate rows, and a multi-hop chain with credentials stripped at both hops. A manifest recorded four hashes: baseline file, repaired file, replay file and the patch itself.
next_hint: The standalone diff applies and replays cleanly. The last risk is the exported evaluator payload: the bundle embeds the diff as a JSON string, so parse the bundle exactly as the external evaluator would, write the extracted diff verbatim, apply it to a fresh pristine tree with git apply --check and apply, compare the modified file hash with the repaired copy, assert the diff targets exactly one file, recompute every manifest hash independently from disk with a deliberate one-line mutation as a negative control, and replay the leak, matrix and multi-hop checks on the bundle-patched tree.
